what: Frame cost at the owner's 1812 stand: the Kinzie household by their boat on the north bank (beside black_jim, about local 1149 E 308 N), 1812-08-14, Full detail, name cards on. Clean dev 285b22502 against this branch, same container, same stand, same 45 s settle.
how: Headless Chromium on ANGLE SwiftShader (no GPU), the page's own animation loop. Every rAF callback timed by wrapping window.requestAnimationFrame; each api layer's update and renderer.render wrapped in performance.now(); the WebGL context's texture and buffer calls counted. 'render off' runs stub renderer.render so the JavaScript columns are not drowned by software rasterising; 'render on' runs draw at 480x300 and count what is uploaded. A SwiftShader millisecond is this container's CPU, not a GPU's: the counts (skeletons, uploads) are machine-free, the milliseconds are for before/after on one machine only.

skeletons_drawn_a_frame.note: 1280x800 screenshot stand: 319 -> 50; 390x780 phone (Light): 736 -> 94, with the same 47 people drawn

texture_uploads_a_frame.note: texSubImage2D; the before set is almost all 16x16 and 20x20 float bone textures, one per skinned piece

before.note: render off, 338 frames; 37.3 ms max with render on

frame_js_less_render_ms.note: render off, 30 s each. The median and p95 are within run-to-run spread (the skeleton work these changes cut runs inside the render, which these columns leave out); the tail is the three-second black-box stall removed.

not_changed_here: A first build's one-off fits (a body's kit map, a garment's nearest-body table) are still one step each; later builds of the same piece reuse them.
The driver draws at the Kinzie stand (about 6,700) and triangles (1.5 M) predate this work (1a6a7f089^: 6,691 and 1.51 M). The GPU side of an Intel UHD 630 cannot be measured in this container.

second_pass.what: Builds in steps (humans.js buildSteps through queueBuild/pumpBuilds; human-variation.js applyVariationSteps a body or garment a step; human-hair.js growHairSteps 128 cards a step) and a posing stride past 30 m (every 2nd frame) and 50 m (every 3rd), with the time between carried (humans.js animateEvery).
second_pass.how: Same container and probe as above: headless Chromium on SwiftShader, render stubbed so the script columns read; 45-60 s settle, 25 s standing. The counts and the before/after on one machine are what hold; the milliseconds are this container's.
